newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends lower on dollar short-covering.

text.p: The won closed lower on Tuesday on the back of dollar shortcovering combined with some building up as the market turned bullish toward the U.S. currency, dealers said.
"As dealers believed an inflow of foreign funds for stock investment ended, they tried to buy the greenback before it rose further," a domestic bank dealer.
A foreign bank dealer said the market remained slightly short on dollars after the central bank soaked up the currency ahead of the foreign share limit expansion last week.
The won closed at 894.80 compared with 893.10 on Friday.
The market closed on Monday for Children's Day.
The won moved in a wide range between 895.70 and 892.00.
"The dollar staged a consolidation before the close," said the foreign bank dealer.

Dealers said the monetary authority seemed to regard the current won/dollar rate as reasonable for the nation's exports. "The rate will move in a boxed range around the 890 won level for the time being. But it is expected to gradually increase," the foreign bank dealer.
Wedensday's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 894.20 against 891.90 today. -- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
